reader.requirement: At --std 85 the values of data-name-1/-3/-4 are read when OPEN OUTPUT executes (first logical page) and again when a WRITE ADVANCING PAGE executes or a page overflow occurs (next logical page), and a change between those times does not affect the current page.
reader.edition-search: Same greps as GR6: no Edition / CobolVersion / DialectBehavior read on the emitter's LinageArg/LinageOpExpr or the connector's page methods. The data-name values ride each statement's LinagePage argument and are adopted only in BeginLinagePage (OPEN OUTPUT) and BeginNextLogicalPage (ADVANCING PAGE, overflow).

reader.notes: Measured on the medium: the page after an overflow takes the new body, top and bottom margins and the page in progress keeps the old ones (its bottom margin is the old 1). ADVANCING PAGE goes through the same BeginNextLogicalPage, so one transition serves both GR7b times.

refuter.evidence: BeginNextLogicalPage travels the rest of the OLD page (old body, old bottom) before EvaluateLinage adopts the new values; the overflow decision in PositionOnLogicalPage uses the old _pageBody. Probe rl1.cob at --std 85: shrinking data-name-1 from 6 to 2 while the counter is at 6 does not overflow the current page (A5 ADVANCING 0 stays LC=6), the next overflow adopts body 2 (A7 LC=2, A8 overflows to LC=1). rl2.cob: data-name-3 top 2 at OPEN, changed to 0 before the first WRITE, still gives page 1 two top lines and later pages none (GR7a/GR7b). cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR7b.
